# Toolbar actions resolve by name, but two actions may share one name

## Context

Neo resolves collaborators by name: `component.Base#getPlugin(name)`, `getController(ntype)`, `getReference(name)`. Toolbar actions already follow that model — `toolbar.Base#getActionItem('close')` returns the action instance, and the dock's header policy addresses `close`, `pop-out`, `lock`, `pin` and `reload` that way — but the model rests on an invariant nobody enforces: a name resolves to *one* action only if no two actions share it. Nothing in `toolbar.Base` refuses a duplicate, so a collision degrades silently to first-match. Operator direction (2026-09-05): the plugin lookup is the mental model for actions, and action names must be unique.

## The Problem

`getActionItem(action)` is `getActionItems().find(item => item.action === action) || null` (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs:577`). Two actions carrying the same `action` name make the second unaddressable and route every intent by that name to the first. Both are host programming errors, and both are silent.

Two consumers already pay for the missing invariant:

- The dock built it locally. `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1096-1120` walks the host's header actions and throws on a missing name, a duplicate name, and a name reserved by an engine flag — the comment says why: "`getActionItem(name)` returns the FIRST match … A duplicate makes one of them unaddressable". The duplicate half of that guard belongs to the toolbar, where it would also cover contributions and every non-dock toolbar.
- `HeaderActionPolicy.mjs:392-400` works around first-match semantics by hand: while the engine `reload` flag is off, a host may own the name `reload`, so the policy returns early rather than write into whatever `getActionItem('reload')` happens to find.

An unnamed action is a second, smaller hole: `getActionItem(undefined)` returns the first action that has no name, so "get by name" can hand back an action nobody named.

## The Architectural Reality

- The action set of one toolbar is closed. Every action instance is minted by `createActionItemConfig` (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs:418`), which stamps `isToolbarAction: true`; `getActionItems()` (`:568`) filters on exactly that flag. Three paths feed it: `syncActions(actions)` (`:623`, the reactive `actions_` config), `createActionItemConfigs`, and `addActionContribution(config)` (`:532`, plugin-owned contributions kept across consumer rebuilds — `tab/plugin/Overflow` is the one contributor). A uniqueness check at `syncActions` and `addActionContribution` therefore covers the whole set.
- `createActionItemConfig` already throws on malformed input — an unknown `actionMap` key, an icon-only action without a name (`:428`, `:442`). Throwing on a duplicate is the same idiom in the same method family.
- String actions carry their name through the `actionMap` factory: `dialog/header/Toolbar.mjs:18` resolves `'close'` to `{action: 'close', …}`. Object actions carry `action` explicitly; the key is copied onto the instance by `Neo.create`, not declared as a config.
- The lookup has one delegate, `tab/Container.mjs:404 getActionItem(action)`, and eleven call lines in `src/` (`code/LivePreview.mjs:395,523`, `dashboard/dock/plugin/Maximize.mjs:757,966`, `dashboard/dock/interaction/RevealOverlay.mjs:499`, `HeaderActionPolicy.mjs:149,176,203,367,399`), plus 105 lines across 20 spec files.
- `getPlugin` has the same first-match shape and no uniqueness guard (`component/Base.mjs:1471`, `beforeSetPlugins :1187`). Out of scope here; noted so the symmetry is deliberate.

## The Fix

1. **Uniqueness, enforced where the set is closed.** A protected `toolbar.Base` helper collects the `action` names of a candidate config list plus the instances that will survive beside them and throws `Neo.toolbar.Base: duplicate toolbar action "<name>"` on a repeat. `syncActions` calls it with the new consumer configs against the surviving contributions before it removes or inserts anything; `addActionContribution` calls it with the one contribution against `getActionItems()` before the spacer or the contribution is inserted, so a refused contribution leaves the toolbar untouched. Unnamed configs are skipped — they cannot be addressed, so they cannot collide.
2. **The lookup takes the family's name.** `toolbar.Base#getAction(name)` replaces `getActionItem(action)`; `tab.Container` delegates under the same name; the eleven `src/` call lines and the spec lines follow (a scripted rename, no behaviour change). `getAction()` with no name returns `null`: an unnamed action is not addressable. `getActionItems()` keeps its name — it is the instance collection, and `getActions()` would collide with the `actions` config accessor.
   Downstream callers outside this repository were not measured from this seat. The implementer greps the private consumer repositories before opening the PR: zero callers means a hard rename; any caller means `getActionItem` stays as a one-line `@deprecated` alias whose docblock names the consumer's migration as its removal trigger.
3. **The dock's copy retires.** The host-vs-host duplicate branch in `LayoutAdapter.mjs:1109-1111` (and its `seen` bookkeeping) goes; the toolbar now throws for the same collision when the projected header receives its actions. The name-required branch (`:1105`) and the reserved-name branch (`:1113`) stay — they are dock policy the toolbar cannot know (intents route by name; engine-owned names are reserved even while their flag is off). The spec arm pinning the deleted branch (`test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockLayoutAdapter.spec.mjs:331`) is replaced by the toolbar arm below.
4. **Spec home:** `test/playwright/unit/toolbar/Actions.spec.mjs`, beside `ActionButton.spec.mjs`, using the `own(Neo.create(Toolbar, {…}))` fixture idiom of `unit/tab/HeaderActions.spec.mjs:71`.

**Decision Record impact:** none. ADR 0029's header-action projection is unchanged; the toolbar invariant is generic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — Constructing a `toolbar.Base` whose `actions` carry two entries with the same `action` name throws an error naming that action; re-assigning `actions` so a consumer action collides with a live contribution throws the same way, and the toolbar's items are unchanged after the throw. Unit arm, red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-2 — `addActionContribution` with a name already present among `getActionItems()` throws before inserting a spacer or the contribution; a distinct name still inserts ahead of consumer actions as today. Unit arm, red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3 — `toolbar.Base#getAction(name)` and `tab.Container#getAction(name)` are the lookups; `grep -rnw "getActionItem" src apps examples test` returns zero lines (the word matcher: `getActionItems`, the collection, stays), or exactly the deprecated alias definition and its docblock when Fix 2's downstream measurement found a caller, with the measurement stated in the PR body.
- [ ] AC-4 — `getAction()` called without a name, or with an empty string, returns `null` even when the toolbar holds an unnamed action. Unit arm, red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-5 — `LayoutAdapter.mjs` no longer throws its own "duplicate host header action" error; the name-required and reserved-name arms in `DockLayoutAdapter.spec.mjs` and `DockLockAction.spec.mjs` are unchanged and green.
- [ ] AC-6 — A `dialog.header.Toolbar` resolves `getAction('close')` to the instance minted by its `actionMap` (the string-action path carries the name). Unit arm.
- [ ] AC-7 — Full unit suite and the `component/dashboard` + `component/tab` component suites green at the PR head (`--workers=1`).

## Out of Scope

- Making `action` mandatory for text actions. Icon-only actions already require a name for their accessible label; a text action without a name keeps working and is simply not addressable.
- A uniqueness guard on `plugins` / `getPlugin`. Same shape, different owner; a sibling ticket if wanted.
- Declaring `action` as a config on `toolbar.ActionButton`; it stays the plain instance key it is today.
- The `actionsState` / change-detection direction of D#18150 Option F. The guard lives in `syncActions`, which every `actions` re-assignment path runs through, so that later work cannot bypass it.

## Avoided Traps

- **Log-and-skip (`manager.Base#register` precedent) rejected.** A skipped action disappears from the toolbar silently — the exact defect shape this ticket removes. Throwing at config time matches how `createActionItemConfig` already treats malformed actions.
- **A permanent alias for `getActionItem` rejected.** Two names for one lookup defeats the mental model the ticket exists for; an alias is admitted only against a measured downstream caller and carries its own removal trigger.
- **`getActions()` as the plural rejected.** It would shadow the `actions` config accessor's meaning (configs) with instances.
- **Keeping the dock's duplicate branch "for the better message" rejected.** One invariant, one owner; the toolbar's error names the toolbar class and the action, and the stack names the projection.
